headline: High-risk shared-workspace and stateful orchestration create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can call APIs and broad network egress, while LangGraph can read/write application files and use stdin/stdout plus developer-defined tools. If Airflow outputs are passed into LangGraph via shared files or stdout, LangGraph may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls.
conditions: IF Airflow output is written into a shared file or queue that LangGraph reads as prompt text
IF LangGraph tool nodes parse upstream content without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add explicit provenance tags to every handoff message
Insert a human review step before LangGraph executes tool-bearing content
Restrict shared files to data-only formats with schema validation
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from Airflow outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing adapters between the systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, and LangGraph can read files and send data to model providers and developer-defined tools. If both touch the same workspace or graph-state store, sensitive file contents can flow from LangGraph into external services or from Airflow into downstream outputs. The profiles do not show isolation or DLP by default.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem, database, or checkpointer store
IF LangGraph forwards file contents to model providers or tools
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Store only minimized, redacted state in the checkpointer
Block sensitive directories from LangGraph file reads
Review outbound destinations for Airflow tasks
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared state and tool outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate external actions over broad network egress, and LangGraph can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write files, and use broad network egress. Even without modify_git_state, both can mutate the same application-defined files or resources, and LangGraph's shared checkpointer increases collision risk. Defaults are dangerous when both operate on shared mutable state.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks and LangGraph nodes write to the same directory or database
IF concurrent runs share the same checkpointer or application-defined files
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories per agent
Use per-run locks around shared resources
Disable concurrent writes to the same checkpointer namespace
Limit LangGraph write access to a scratch directory
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate or route task outputs, and LangGraph is a stateful orchestrator that can consume those outputs as node inputs and trigger tools. If LangGraph treats Airflow-produced facts as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions across multiple steps. The pair has no documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF LangGraph uses Airflow outputs as direct node inputs without validation
IF downstream LangGraph nodes can send emails, modify files, or call external tools based on those inputs
mitigations: Add a verification node before any action-taking step
Require structured schemas for Airflow-to-LangGraph handoffs
Log and diff intermediate outputs before execution
Gate irreversible actions behind approval
requires-engineering: implement end-to-end assertion checks

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is source-available and broadly networked, while LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and application-defined graph state. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or DPA controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data enters the shared workflow. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling and transport paths.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Airflow tasks into LangGraph state
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared workflow
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention and residency for shared state
Redact secrets before passing data between agents
Review vendor and deployment region settings
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
